title: Operations Assistant - Stock, Purchasing & Logistics
description:
Operations Assistant (Stock, Purchasing & Logistics)
East Leeds - Hybrid working available after probation
£30,000 - £35,000 Permanent Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm

A well-established and growing business is looking for an Operations Administrator to join its Operations team overseeing the Stock and Purchasing side of the business.

This is a varied role combining stock administration, purchasing, supplier management, order processing and logistics coordination. You'll be responsible for keeping stock information accurate, monitoring orders and deliveries, resolving queries and working closely with internal teams and external suppliers.

The role would suit an experienced administrator who enjoys working with systems, stock, orders and suppliers and is looking for a long-term opportunity within a friendly and established business.

What's on offer?
- £30,000 - £35,000 salary
- Permanent position
- Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm, 37.5 hours per week
- Hybrid working available after probation, with the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days per week
- Annual bonus scheme
- 25 days' holiday, increasing with length of service
- Option to purchase additional annual leave
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Cycle to work scheme
- Free office parking
- Enhanced sick pay
- Life assurance
- Smart casual dress code

The Role

Working as part of the Operations team, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating incoming stock and monitoring expected delivery dates
- Updating internal systems with stock and supplier information
- Checking supplier pricing and investigating discrepancies
- Raising and processing purchase and stock orders
- Monitoring outstanding orders and deliveries
- Liaising with suppliers to ensure orders are delivered as expected
- Coordinating the movement and processing of stock where required
- Assisting with regular stock checks and system reconciliations
- Investigating and resolving stock, order and invoice queries
- Monitoring customer and supplier orders through to completion
- Supporting internal processes relating to product information and certification
- Working with internal teams to improve systems and processes
- Providing information and updates to colleagues across the business
- Working closely with the sales team to ensure excellent customer service
- Providing general administrative support to the Operations function

About You

We're looking for someone who is organised, commercially aware and comfortable working with stock, orders, suppliers and computer systems.

You will ideally have:

Previous experience in an administrative, stock, purchasing, logistics, supply chain or order processing role
Experience working with a stock, purchasing, inventory or ERP system
Good understanding of administrative and order management processes
Strong attention to detail and good numerical skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Confident telephone manner
Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel
Strong organisational and time management skills
Ability to work accurately in a busy environment
Good problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate and resolve issues
Ability to work independently and use your own initiative
A positive, flexible approach and the ability to work well as part of a team
Experience within a technical, manufacturing, construction, distribution or supply-chain environment would be advantageous, although this is not essential.

Travel

The role is primarily office based in East Leeds.

There will be occasional travel to other UK locations for stock checks, approximately 6 times per year. These visits will generally involve 1-2 overnight stays, with accommodation and business expenses paid by the company.

A full UK driving licence is preferred.

Working Pattern

Monday - Friday, 8.30am - 5pm, with a one-hour lunch break.

The position is initially office based, with 1-2 days' home working available following successful completion of probation, subject to line manager approval.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator looking to develop their career within stock, purchasing, logistics or operations with an established and supportive employer.

Please note that due to the volume of applications we receive, we are only able to respond to candidates who are shortlisted. If you haven't received a response within 48 hours, please assume you have been unsuccessful.

title: Logistics & Purchasing Administrator
description:
Logistics & Purchasing Administrator
Location: Stoke-on-Trent
Salary:Up to £26,500 DOE
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30am - 5:00pm

About the Role

We are currently recruiting for an Logistics & Purchasing Administrator to join a well-established and growing business based in Stoke-on-Trent.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised, proactive and detail-focused individual looking to develop their career within a busy operations environment. Working as part of the Operations team, you will provide essential administrative support across both Logistics and Purchasing, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient running of day-to-day operations.

The successful candidate will be confident communicating with internal teams, customers, suppliers and external partners, while being able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

Logistics
- Provide general administrative support to the Logistics function
- Coordinate courier, pallet network, haulage and specialist vehicle bookings
- Track deliveries, obtain proof of deliveries (PODs) and follow up outstanding shipments
- Investigate delivery issues, damages, shortages and service failures

- Support logistics KPI reporting, route planning and vehicle compliance administration
- Assist with continuous improvement initiatives and logistics projects

Purchasing & Stock
- Produce purchase requirements and stock replenishment reports
- Monitor purchase orders and chase outstanding deliveries
- Use business data to identify large projects and potential stock requirements
- Support supplier performance monitoring and maintain accurate purchasing records
- Assist with stock valuation, inventory analysis and stock counts
- Investigate stock discrepancies and support corrective actions
- Monitor and report on slow-moving and obsolete stock
- Maintain accurate cost prices and purchasing information within business systems
- Provide administrative support for supplier relationship management
- Support product traceability reporting and maintain associated records

You will ideally have:
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- A proactive and ambitious approach, with a desire to learn and progress
- Confident communication skills, both face-to-face and over the telephone
- Excellent customer service skills, with a focus on both internal and external customers
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively
- The ability to remain calm and professional under pressure
- A flexible and adaptable approach to work
- A collaborative and positive attitude
- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to find effective solutions
- Enthusiasm, commitment and reliability
- A professional and confident manner
- A willingness to undertake training and development where required

Qualifications & Core Skills
- GCSEs or equivalent, including English and Maths at Grade C/4 or above
- Good IT literacy, including Microsoft Word and Excel
- Previous administration experience is desirable
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Good customer and people skills
- Excellent organisational skills
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Self-motivated with a proactive approach

title: Business Support Officer
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated, organised and proactive Business Support Officer to join our friendly and forward-thinking GP Practice on a permanent basis. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Primary Care administrator who has a good understanding of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF), Enhanced Services, CQRS and primary care data quality. The successful candidate will work closely with the Practice Management Team and clinical staff, providing specialist support with QOF and Enhanced Services monitoring, searches, reporting, recalls, audits and claims. A key aspect of the role will be ensuring that patient information, clinical coding and activity are accurately recorded so that the Practice can achieve its contractual requirements and maximise Practice income. We are looking for someone who is confident working with data, has excellent attention to detail and is able to take ownership of their workload. The successful candidate will be proactive in identifying areas requiring action and will work collaboratively with the wider Practice team to achieve positive outcomes. The postholder will: Support the Management Team with the delivery and monitoring of QOF and Enhanced Services. Run regular searches using EMIS Web and Ardens Manager. Monitor QOF and Enhanced Services performance on a monthly basis. Identify areas of underachievement or outstanding activity and work with the relevant Practice staff to address these. Prepare and submit national and local CQRS claims, ensuring all claims are accurate and submitted within required deadlines. Support and monitor the Practice's recall system, particularly for patients with long-term conditions. Identify patients requiring reviews, monitoring, investigations or other relevant interventions. Undertake regular checks of patient records to ensure clinical information and activity are accurately recorded. Support clinicians and administrative staff with clinical coding and data quality. Identify and correct data quality issues which could affect QOF, Enhanced Services or other commissioned income. Ensure appropriate coding and recording of activity to support accurate reporting and maximise Practice income. Undertake audits and analyse Practice data to identify trends, gaps and areas for improvement. Complete and submit reporting templates and data returns for the ICS, PCN and other relevant organisations. Maintain accurate spreadsheets, monitoring tools and records relating to QOF, Enhanced Services, recalls, audits and reporting. Provide regular performance information and updates to the Practice Management Team. Support the Practice Management Team with the delivery and monitoring of QOF and Enhanced Services. Liaise with clinicians, Practice staff, PCN colleagues and external organisations as required. Provide general administrative and business support to the Practice Management Team. Undertake other duties appropriate to the role as required. About the Candidate We are seeking an individual who is highly organised, self-motivated and able to work proactively with minimal supervision. You will have excellent attention to detail and understand the importance of accurate data, clinical coding and timely completion of contractual requirements. You will ideally have previous experience working in General Practice and be familiar with QOF, Enhanced Services, EMIS Web, Ardens Manager and CQRS. The ability to analyse data, identify areas requiring action and communicate effectively with both clinical and non-clinical colleagues is essential. Knowledge of clinical coding would be particularly advantageous, as the postholder will play an important role in ensuring the accuracy and completeness of coding to support QOF and Enhanced Services achievement.
